SELECTED_INDEX: 1  
CONFIDENCE: 0.25  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by a very intense band at 648 cm⁻¹, a position that is characteristic of the C–S stretching mode of sulfoxides (e.g. the well-known 671 cm⁻¹ Raman line of DMSO).  
Candidate 1 (O=S1OCCO1) is a five-membered cyclic sulfoxide and therefore contains a single S–O(=O) center bonded to carbon, exactly the functional group that gives rise to this strong Raman line.  
Additional supporting peaks:  
• 1023 cm⁻¹ – fits the S=O stretching vibration of sulfoxides (typical 1010–1030 cm⁻¹).  
• 805 cm⁻¹ – compatible with ring O–C–O skeletal vibrations of a 1,3-dioxathiolane ring.  
• 535–575 cm⁻¹ – weaker C–S/O–S deformations often observed in sulfoxide rings.  
• 1231, 1282 and 1437 cm⁻¹ together with C–H stretches at 2854–2972 cm⁻¹ match CH₂/CH bends and stretches expected for a small aliphatic ring.  

Among the candidates, only molecule 1 simultaneously offers a sulfoxide (to explain the 648 cm⁻¹ and 1023 cm⁻¹ bands) and the simple aliphatic framework that accounts for the remaining peaks, making it the best match.
